physicalNotes: Radius 0.45231588 Jupiter radii from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A.209Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract): 32,337 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0711 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Yalçinkaya et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A.209Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname YALCINKAYA_ET_AL_2025): P 3.855219 d
sources.shape: Yalçinkaya et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A.209Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname YALCINKAYA_ET_AL_2025): a/R* 14.99; Yalçinkaya et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A.209Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname YALCINKAYA_ET_AL_2025): inclination 88.68 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Yalçinkaya et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A.209Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname YALCINKAYA_ET_AL_2025): transit mid-time 2459856.48875 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 2 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
